title: Align tenant contract, API doc, frontend types and design doc with the shipped surface
goal: Several documents describe a tenant surface that is not the one that ships. TENANT_API.md documents a GET /system/tenant/:id/members/page compatibility alias that exists only in the unmounted tenant_routes.go, and shows create/update/delete responses as a bare message object while the handler returns the common envelope. MemberUsageQuery.status is typed 'active' | 'removed' while the UI sends 'disabled', hidden by a cast. MULTI_TENANT_DESIGN.md still describes subdomains, custom domains, branding and public registration as a next phase, none of which is in the V1 contract. The contract says owner transfer is an explicit API action but no transfer endpoint exists; the shipped path is add-owner then remove-owner. This wave changes documentation and one type union, no runtime behaviour.
findings: TC-05 (P3): TENANT_API.md:229,255 document /system/tenant/:id/members/page as a live compatibility alias; the route is registered only in tenant_routes.go:25, and RegisterRoutes/NewHandler have no production caller.
TC-05 (P3): TENANT_API.md:153-157 and :169-174 show create/update/delete responses as {"message": ...}; tenant_platform_handler.go:143,163,178 return common.Success with an envelope.
TC-06 (P3): api.ts:239 types status as 'active' | 'removed'; TenantMemberList.tsx:230-236 sends 'disabled'; the cast at :84 hides the mismatch.
TC-08 (P3): MULTI_TENANT_DESIGN.md describes subdomains, custom domains, branding and public registration as an implementation phase; TENANT_CONTRACT_V1.md section 1 puts them out of scope.
TC-07 wording: TENANT_CONTRACT_V1.md section 2.2 says owner transfer is an explicit API action; the service exposes add-owner and remove-owner but no transfer endpoint.

in: Remove the /members/page compatibility-alias paragraphs from TENANT_API.md and state that only /members is mounted
Align the create/update/delete response examples in TENANT_API.md with the common envelope actually returned
Update the delete, add-member and switchable sections to the behaviour landed by W1, W2 and W4
Change MemberUsageQuery.status to 'active' | 'disabled' and remove the cast in TenantMemberList.tsx
Add a status banner to the top of docs/designs/MULTI_TENANT_DESIGN.md: vision document, not a V1 commitment; the binding scope is TENANT_CONTRACT_V1.md section 1
Rewrite the owner-transfer sentence in contract section 2.2 to describe the shipped two-step path (add a second owner, then remove the previous one) and state that no single transfer endpoint exists
Add a revision note to the contract recording the W1/W2/W4 clarifications, without changing any invariant
out: Adding a transfer endpoint or any other runtime change
Rewriting the whole design document or deleting it
Changing permission codes, menus, i18n keys or routes
Aligning documents to behaviour the dependent waves have not landed yet (run this wave afterwards)

implementationNotes: Documentation must describe the shipped behaviour, not the intended one. If a dependent wave was abandoned, document the surviving behaviour and say so.
The status union change is type-only; do not change what the UI sends at runtime.
For the design document, add a banner and a short 'what is not in V1' list that points at the contract; do not delete the exploratory content.
The contract revision note must be additive: clarify wording, do not re-open the In/Out boundary.
Run check-doc-links and check-doc-inventory after editing; removing the alias paragraph must leave no dangling anchor.

executionRoles.implementerPosture: Read the landed code first, then edit the documents to match it; change only the type union in source.
reviewerPosture: Spot-check every edited example against a real handler response.
Confirm no documented route is absent from system_modules.go.
Confirm the type union matches every value the UI sends.
Confirm the design banner names the binding contract.
Confirm the contract change is a clarification, not a scope change.

runtimeEvidence: one real response body for create, update and delete captured from a running instance, or an explicit not-run with the environment gap

baseline recorded on 2026-10-27: backend build/vet and 46 packages of tests pass; frontend tsc, eslint and build (including the 14 prebuild contract checks) pass, so this wave starts from a green tree

humanGates: Approve the contract revision note; it clarifies owner transfer and multi-membership without changing the In/Out boundary.
completionChecklist: TENANT_API.md documents only mounted routes and the real envelope

MULTI_TENANT_DESIGN.md is marked as a vision document
Contract section 2.2 describes the shipped owner-transfer path
Doc link and inventory gates pass
